## Highlights

  * •

IDDES is employed to investigate propeller wake evolution under varying bottom-boundary clearances.

  * •

Bottom-boundary confinement induces premature wake instability and accelerates tip-vortex breakdown.

  * •

Wall proximity distorts helical vortex trajectories and enhances wake asymmetry and vortex deformation.

  * •

Strong confinement intensifies near-bed pressure fluctuation, wall shear scouring, and turbulent mixing.

  * •

PSD analysis reveals accelerated coherence loss and earlier broadband spectral evolution under confinement.

## Abstract

This study uses IDDES with the SST k-ω model to investigate the wake of the CNR-INM E779A propeller under rigid bottom-wall confinement. Three bottom-clearance cases are considered, with open-water flow used as a reference. The analysis focuses on hydrodynamic loading, vortex–wall interaction, wake transition, and turbulence development. The results show that reducing the clearance increases load fluctuations and strengthens the unsteady response of the propeller. Strong confinement accelerates the loss of tip-vortex coherence, promotes earlier wake destabilization, and leads to more intense vortex–wall impingement. These effects produce disordered near-wall loading, disrupted streamline topology, and faster breakdown of coherent vortical structures. In contrast, larger clearances allow the wake to remain more organized over a longer downstream distance. Turbulence statistics further indicate earlier growth of turbulent kinetic energy, stronger Reynolds-stress redistribution, and enhanced turbulence anisotropy under reduced clearance. Spectral results confirm a faster decay of blade-passing-frequency signatures and an earlier transition toward broadband turbulence. These findings clarify how bottom-wall proximity modifies propeller wake instability and turbulent momentum transport, providing guidance for shallow-water propulsion and near-bottom marine operations.

## Graphical abstract

This graphical abstract illustrates the evolutionary mechanism of a marine propeller wake under wall confinement via high-fidelity IDDES simulations. It sequentially presents the physical chain from propeller load fluctuations, to vortex dynamics and vortex-wall interaction, to turbulence characteristics (including turbulent kinetic energy and Reynolds stresses), and finally to power spectral density (PSD). The results reveal that wall distance significantly regulates the wake instability, turbulent energy transfer and spectral evolution, providing a visualized insight into the near-wall propeller wake dynamics.Image

Title: HEP Statistical Inference for UAV Fault Detection: CLs, LRT, and SBI Applied to Blade Damage
Authors: Khushiyant
Date: Thu Mar 19 07:01:09 2026

This paper transfers three statistical methods from particle physics to multirotor propeller fault detection: the likelihood ratio test (LRT) for binary detection, the CLs modified frequentist method for false alarm rate control, and sequential neural posterior estimation (SNPE) for quantitative fault characterization. Operating on spectral features tied to rotor harmonic physics, the system returns three outputs: binary detection, controlled false alarm rates, and calibrated posteriors over fault severity and motor location. On UAV-FD, a hexarotor dataset of 18 real flights with 5% and 10% blade damage, leave-one-flight-out cross-validation gives AUC 0.862 +/- 0.007 (95% CI: 0.849--0.876), outperforming CUSUM (0.708 +/- 0.010), autoencoder (0.753 +/- 0.009), and LSTM autoencoder (0.551). At 5% false alarm rate the system detects 93% of significant and 81% of subtle blade damage. On PADRE, a quadrotor platform, AUC reaches 0.986 after refitting only the generative models. SNPE gives a full posterior over fault severity (90% credible interval coverage 92--100%, MAE 0.012), so the output includes uncertainty rather than just a point estimate or fault flag. Per-flight sequential detection achieves 100% fault detection with 94% overall accuracy.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
